question_en:
I previously saved the attached image from Chandra's 2014 Multiwavelength Images feature, but I did not note the specific page. Now, I want to select another composite image from the same year's feature to explain to students: why does a single distant object appear as multiple images around a foreground galaxy? Please answer the following questions in order.

1. **Identify the object in the attachment.** What is the name of the object shown in the attachment?

2. Among all image cards on the "2014 Chandra Images With Multiwavelength Feature" annual page, which image card has four pink bright spots next to a golden ring-like structure in the center, arranged with "three on one side and one on the opposite side"? Please provide the name of the object in that image card. View only the default Composite images on each detail page.

Answer format: Provide the name of the object in the attachment for Question 1 and the name of the object meeting the image conditions for Question 2 in text.
answer:
Question 1: Flame Nebula (NGC 2024).

Question 2: RX J1131-1231.
